references.text: The same procedure of burning the bull outside the camp—its skin, flesh, and dung—is repeated during the consecration of Aaron and his sons
The flesh and skin were burned with fire outside the camp as part of the sin offering on the day of consecration
On the Day of Atonement, the sin offering bull and the sin offering goat, including their skin, flesh, and dung, were to be burned outside the camp
During the priestly consecration, the bull's flesh, skin, and dung were to be burned with fire outside the camp as a sin offering
The red heifer was to be burned along with its skin, flesh, blood, and dung in connection with the water for cleansing
The book of Hebrews points out that the animals sacrificed for sin were burned outside the camp, linking this to Jesus suffering outside the city gate
